title: Degraded stock lookups: orders-api latency tracked memory usage
symptoms: elevated p95 latency on the alerting service
callers seeing timeouts and 5xx once the process was under heap pressure
RSS well above the usual band for that service
process memory usage climbing for tens of minutes
observed_signals: after a restart, memory dropped and then began climbing again
CPU increased only moderately until GC became frequent
memory_usage rose smoothly over a long period rather than in a single jump

timeline.event: a deploy or flag change on orders-api that populated a new cache
memory_usage on orders-api began a near-linear climb
GC / heap warnings became frequent on orders-api
error-rate or latency alert fired on orders-api
a second climb started until the code fix landed

contributing_factors: an in-process cache had no eviction policy
the growth was slow enough that a 15-minute baseline looked almost normal at first
resolution: restarted the affected deployment as immediate mitigation
identified an unbounded in-process cache with no TTL
shipped a hotfix with eviction and a heap-growth alert
lessons_learned: caches without TTL belong on the review checklist for every service
a restart that restores latency is mitigation, not a fix
